stem:
A ward medical officer reviews a patient admitted with vomiting and dehydration. Urine output has remained above 0.5 mL/kg/hour throughout. The same laboratory reports the following creatinine results.

| Time | Creatinine | Reference interval |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Admission | 62 µmol/L | 45–100 µmol/L |
| 36 hours later | 90 µmol/L | 45–100 µmol/L |

How should the trend be interpreted?

options.label: A
options.text: Not AKI, because the rise is less than 1.5 times baseline
options.explanation: The rise is 1.45 times baseline, below the 1.5-fold criterion, but that is only one of the KDIGO criteria. Meeting any one criterion defines AKI.

options.label: B
options.text: AKI, because the 48-hour rise exceeds the absolute threshold
options.explanation: Creatinine rose by 28 µmol/L within 48 hours, which meets the KDIGO criterion of a rise of at least 26.5 µmol/L in 48 hours. This is stage 1 AKI even though both values are within the reference interval.

options.label: C
options.text: Not AKI, because both results lie within the reference interval
options.explanation: A reference interval describes a population. A rise within it can still represent a substantial loss of this patient's kidney function.

options.label: D
options.text: Not AKI, because urine output has stayed above the threshold
options.explanation: Urine output is one criterion and creatinine another. Normal urine output does not exclude AKI defined by creatinine.

options.label: E
options.text: Stage 2 AKI, because creatinine has risen by almost half
options.explanation: Stage 2 requires creatinine to reach 2.0–2.9 times baseline. A rise of less than 1.5 times, meeting the absolute criterion, is stage 1.

context: AKI is defined by any one KDIGO criterion: a rise of at least 26.5 µmol/L within 48 hours, a rise to 1.5 times baseline within 7 days, or reduced urine output.
